videos.title: OPINIONS ARE CONCEPTS. IF THEY ARE STRONGLY LINKED TO YOUR EGO, YOU WILL BE EASILY OFFENDED.
videos.description:
Eckhart Tolle- world revered teacher on consciousness, explains. On the Huberman Lab podcast out now.

On the podcast, Tolle also explains some practices that you can use to observe where your ego starts and stops. Ego is important for striving, but if it’s too strongly attached to certain concepts, it makes you vulnerable to be offended by anything/one that disagrees with you.

In some ways, feeling flattered is just as dangerous/a reflection of a concept attached ego. (If people agreeing with you makes you feel too good, it’s also a sign that your ego is too strongly tethered to concepts.)

Eckhart explains that the goal is to not be detached or to meditate all the time, but rather to be able to understand why certain things bother you and to see the distinction between concepts linked to ego and concepts as a separate thing.

NOTE: Most of the episode focuses on practical tools to lean into life with more presence and calm and to experience relationships, nature, and your internal landscape with more peace and joy.

It is quickly turning on to be one of our more popular episodes.

videos.title: The Only Question to Ask Before Marrying
videos.description:
Harvard photography students once took part in a study about choosing. Each one made several prints and picked a favorite to keep.

Half were told the pick was final. The other half could swap it over the next few days.

Psychologist Dan Gilbert tracked how they felt about their choice. The students who couldn't switch grew more attached to their photo. The ones who could switch didn't. And almost nobody in that group changed their mind. Just having the option kept them from settling in.

Marriage runs on the same machinery. Keep one foot out the door and you'll keep grading your partner against people you haven't met. Every dull evening starts to look like proof you picked wrong.

Committing changes how you see the person across the table. The conversation gets easier to enjoy once you stop auditioning other ones.

That's no excuse to marry the wrong person. But once you've found someone you like talking to, stop holding on to the receipt.

So picture yourself at 80. Who do you want across the table?
